title: Figure 2.8: Wright's puppy birth-weight path diagram
content: Wright's birth-weight model separates the direct effect of gestation period from the noncausal association induced by litter size through prenatal growth rate.

variables.name: Other causes of growth rate (A)
variables.content: Unobserved exogenous causes of prenatal growth rate other than litter size.

variables.name: Litter size (L)
variables.content: The measured number of pups sharing the pregnancy.

variables.name: Other causes of gestation period (C)
variables.content: Unobserved exogenous causes of gestation period other than litter size.

variables.name: Prenatal growth rate (Q)
variables.content: The unobserved rate at which the pup grows in utero.

variables.name: Gestation period (P)
variables.content: The measured length of time the pup spends in utero.

variables.name: Birth weight (X)
variables.content: The pup's measured weight at birth.

arrows.because: Figure 2.8 shows unobserved causes A entering prenatal growth rate Q with coefficient a.
Figure 2.8 shows litter size L entering prenatal growth rate Q with coefficient l.
Figure 2.8 shows litter size L entering gestation period P with coefficient l-prime.
Figure 2.8 shows unobserved causes C entering gestation period P with coefficient c.
Figure 2.8 shows prenatal growth rate Q entering birth weight X with coefficient q.
Figure 2.8 shows gestation period P entering birth weight X with direct-effect coefficient p.

linear_correlations.content: The source reports that one additional gestation day is associated with 5.66 grams of birth weight, while warning that this observed correlation is not the direct effect.
